gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-cypro-minoan: Silkscreen spaces its letters out so loosely you can almost feel the gaps, and every line it draws is uniform, with no thin parts at all. Noto Sans Cypro Minoan is the sans-serif that does the quieter work, its terminals cut back to leave a generous gap.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-hatran: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen lays its letters out like strands of spaghetti, each stroke the same thickness from end to end. And Noto Sans Hatran follows with an approachable, funnel-throated e, so the page moves from novelty to ease.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-inscriptiona: Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi reads as approachable and contemporary, with small counters that never feel clogged. Silkscreen sits above it looking thin yet having no thinner parts anywhere, and Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi lets that lo-fi heading breathe.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-javanese: Silkscreen keeps its curves full, never thinning at a turn. Noto Sans Javanese below is clean and neutral, its apertures linking each counter to the space outside, so the retro heading gets a quiet partner.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Silkscreen's stems match its hairlines, because it has none. Noto Sans Kawi gives that retro heading a clean, neutral partner, its open-jawed c like a pair of pliers keeping the text lines easy to follow.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-linear-b: Modern and neutral in the text, but the heading goes lo-fi: Silkscreen swaps hairline joins for full-width stroke connections. Noto Sans Linear B just glides around each bend.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-manichaean: Modern and clean, Noto Sans Manichaean is the body here. Silkscreen has no calligraphic shading to guide the eye, so Noto Sans Manichaean, with open-mouthed e crossbars, carries the reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-mongolian: Silkscreen glows like neon glass tubing, lo-fi and retro, with generous space around every single letter. Noto Sans Mongolian simply reads, its terminals flaring outward.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-new-tai-lue: Noto Sans New Tai Lue reads as neutral and modern, its round letters looking cupped rather than clenched. Silkscreen is best at outlining counters in one steady thickness, while this sans-serif handles the reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-nko: Noto Sans NKo is modern and contemporary, with openings you can see through, and it sits under a retro heading. But Silkscreen draws its letters as if with a round-tipped pen, which gives the plain sans its contrast.
